top_signal.title: I think reaching out to applicants as fast as you reach back out to leads makes a massive difference
top_signal.summary: I own a cleaning company. For a long time, when a lead came in, whoever was free would call them back. Sometimes that was an hour later, sometimes the next day. Eventually we set it up so every inbound lead gets a call back right away, and revenue went up as you could likely predict. We weren't getting more leads. We were just slow before, and some of them went with whoever called first.   I've been thinking about this with hiring lately. If you hire hourly people you probably already know they apply to a bunch of places at once and take whoever calls first with an actual shift. It's basically the same problem.   The applicant version is pretty simple. Send a text as soon as the application comes in with a real time you'll call, and then actually call in that window. If it comes in at night, make it the first call the next morning. Try a couple more times over the next two days before you write them off.   Anyway, its been helping us land a lot of quality cleaning service providers. Does anyone else here have a similar process?        submitted by     /u/Mike-Runs-Ops       [link]       [comments]
